idiom_name: wrapper component with a RenderFragment/ChildContent parameter, or Func<T,T> composition
implementation_notes: C# supplies the composition half for free (System.Func<T,T> plus extension methods), but Blazor has no enhancer API: a component is a class deriving from ComponentBase, and the reusable form of 'add behaviour to many components' is a hand-written wrapper component that receives the wrapped content as a RenderFragment (ChildContent) or wraps a component type and applies the concern in its lifecycle methods. Use a Func-based enhancer when the concern is pure data (feature gating, authorization decisions over parameters); use the wrapper component when the concern must live inside the render tree. The wrapper component stays the right answer for anything that must exist as a component - boundaries, cascading values, layout - because only a component can participate in rendering.
code_sketch:
// enhancer over a component factory: Func<T,T>
public static Func<ComponentBase> WithLogging(Func<ComponentBase> make) =>
    () => { var c = make(); Logger.Log(c.GetType().Name); return c; };

@* wrapper component: the reusable form inside the render tree *@
<WithAuthorization Role="admin">
    <ReportsPage />
</WithAuthorization>
pitfalls: A wrapper component adds a render-tree level and its own lifecycle: parameters arrive after the first render, so derived state belongs in OnParametersSet or later, not in the constructor.
RenderFragment delegates capture the parent's render context, so a wrapper cannot stop the wrapped content from re-rendering when the parent does.
Cascading values and DI are resolved per component: a wrapper that does not re-publish them hides the outer scope from everything it wraps.
